chunks: Dorost ibn Abī Manṣūr narrated to me that he asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام.
Was Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله constrained by Abū Ṭālib?
So he عليه السلام said: No. Rather, he was entrusted with the bequests, so he handed them over to him صلى الله عليه وآله.
He said: I said, then did he hand over the bequests to him on the basis that he was constrained by him?
So he عليه السلام said: If he had been constrained by him, he would not have handed the bequest over to him.
He said: So I said, then what was the state of Abū Ṭālib?
He عليه السلام said: He affirmed the Prophet and that which he brought, and he handed the bequests over to him, and he died that very day.

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: he affirmed and acknowledged as true
key_terms.الْوَصَايَا: the bequests or entrusted legacies passed onward
key_terms.بِالنَّبِيِّ: with respect to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.مَحْجُوجًا: being subject to another's proof, authority, or decisive claim
key_terms.مُسْتَوْدَعًا: entrusted as a repository or custodian

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kāfī narrate about the faith and status of Abū Ṭālib?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the status of Abū Ṭālib in relation to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and clarifies that the Prophet was not under his proof or authority. Rather, Abū Ṭālib was entrusted with the bequests and transferred them to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It also states that Abū Ṭālib affirmed the Prophet and what he brought before his death.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Saeed Bin Abdullah, from a group of our companions,from Ahmad Bin Hilal, from Amayya Bin Ali Al Qaysi who said, 
‘Dorost Bin Abu Mansour narrated to me that he asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup>, ‘Was Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> (ever) cautioned by Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, he<sup>asws</sup> was a repository of the bequest, so he<sup>asws</sup> handed it over to him<sup>saww</sup>’. I said, ‘So he<sup>as</sup> handed over the bequest to him<sup>saww</sup> upon that he<sup>saww</sup> was incapacitated by him<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Had he<sup>saww</sup> been incapacitated by him<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> would not have handed over the bequest to him<sup>saww</sup>’.
So I said, ‘So what was the state of Abu Talib<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup>?’

He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘He<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> acknowledge with the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and with whatever he<sup>saww</sup> came with, and handed over the bequest, and passed away on that day’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Sa‘d ibn ‘Abdallah from a group of our people from Ahmad ibn Hilal from ’Umayya ibn Ali al-Qaysi who has said that narrated to me Durust ibn abu Mansur who has said the following.
“ I once asked abu al-Hassan (a.s.), ‘Did the Messenger of Allah receive any authority from abu Talib (a.s.) ?”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “No, but abu Talib was the trustee of certain (items) that he delivered to the Holy Prophet (s.a.) .
” I then asked, “What was the condition of abu Talib?”
He acknowledged the Holy Prophet (s.a.) and his Divine message. He delivered to him the (Items of) will and died on that day.”
